messages:
Alex W: Kicking off Zenith POC — they want TGW multipath with PrivateLink as primary, plus a Hosted fallback. Also security questionnaire + rough cost for a 2TB egress POC.

Morgan L: Quick note — TGW multipath depends on attachment/route config. PrivateLink is per-subnet ENIs. Multipath at TGW layer may split across attachments but session stickiness usually preserved by 5-tuple.

Sarah P: Zenit's security asks: no TLS inspection (they want passthrough), SNI preservation, and static firewall allowlist for the POC.

Calvin (SE): For PrivateLink (interface endpoints) traffic originates from their VPC to our endpoint ENI inside their subnet. That means egress/source IPs are under their control (NAT/EIP). We don't provide fixed public IPs on PrivateLink.

NetOps-Jess: If they require static egress IPs from their side for their downstream firewall, advise them to allocate EIPs on NAT gateways per AZ.

Morgan L: Pricing callout — PrivateLink has per-GB data processing and hourly endpoint costs; TGW has attachment and data transfer fees. Our Hosted vs Dedicated billing for traffic depends on deployment model. See internal pricing summary: https://redwood.in/pricing/private-connect (share after call).

Alex W: Can someone sketch a simple cost ballpark for 2TB egress + interface endpoint uptime for one month so we can share with Zenith?

Calvin (SE): I'll do a quick calc. Assumptions: us-east-1, PrivateLink data processing $0.01/GB (example), hourly endpoint $0.01/hr. 2TB = ~2048GB -> ~$20.48 data processing + endpoint (~$7) => ~ $30-$40 AWS infra cost on top of our usage fees. Will break out exact numbers in a spreadsheet.

Sarah P: Security questionnaire bit: they asked for a list of ports/hostnames we need them to allow. Also whether we support mTLS for connector auth.

Calvin (SE): Minimal network requirements: outbound/inbound depends on topology, but we usually need TCP/443 for API traffic. Sample snippet to give them:

```
Allow outbound TCP 443 to:
- api.redwood-inference.com (FQDN list will be provided)
If using PrivateLink: allow ENI IPs in the subnets you create for the endpoint.
VPN fallback: allow UDP 500, UDP 4500 (IPSec/NAT-T)
```

Morgan L: Note — we can provide an FQDN CSV and a recommended ephemeral IP list for quick allowlisting, but emphasize PrivateLink ENIs live in their subnet so IPs are customer-managed.

NetOps-Jess: Also ensure there are no overlapping CIDRs between their TGW/spokes and our Private deployment subnets. For Private deployments we recommend unique /16 allocation per customer to avoid accidental overlap.

Alex W: Is canary/fallback routing to Hosted supported if PrivateLink path fails? Their app demands high availability during POC.

Calvin (SE): Yes — control plane supports route policies: Primary = PrivateLink, Fallback = Hosted (TLS over internet). Failover is transparent to the app but expect a brief reconnection window; latency delta depends on region (~50-200ms). We can show a sample policy config.

Sarah P: On TLS: they insist on end-to-end TLS termination on their proxy (no inspection). Can we preserve SNI and do passthrough?

Calvin (SE): We can do passthrough and preserve SNI. If they want mutual auth we support mTLS between their proxy and our connector — requires cert exchange steps documented in the SOW.

DeployBot: Ticket created: PROJ-4123 "Zenith POC connectivity + pricing calc" (assignee: Calvin (SE))

Alex W: Action items:
- Calvin: detailed pricing spreadsheet + route policy example (EOD)
- Morgan: FQDN allowlist CSV and brief pricing blurb for sales deck
- Jess: note on NAT/EIP and CIDR guidance for NetOps handoff
- Sarah: send the redwood sample security questionnaire answers to Zenith

Zenith-IT: (external) Quick clarifying Q: for TGW multipath, can traffic egress from multiple AZs and will that break our client affinity?

Calvin (SE): TGW multipath can egress across attachments in different AZs but session affinity is maintained by hashing on 5-tuple; for long-lived connections recommend ensuring stickiness on their proxy side.

Zenith-IT: Also planning a VPN fallback. Confirm we need UDP 500/4500 open on our firewall?

NetOps-Jess: Yes — allow UDP 500 and 4500 for S2S IPSec (NAT-T). If you use a managed VPN, check provider docs for additional ports.

Alex W: I’ll schedule a technical handoff call for Tue 10am PT and share the calc + docs beforehand. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Calvin (SE): Will upload the spreadsheet to PROJ-4123 and ping once done.

Morgan L: I’ll prepare the FQDN list and add a small narrative around variable costs for the deck.

Sarah P: Sending the completed security QN to Zenith after the call.

Zenith-IT: Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround.
